claims.title: Rise of the Yamato state
claims.summary: Clan leaders on the Yamato plain consolidate power, build monumental kofun tombs, and establish the imperial lineage claiming descent from the sun goddess Amaterasu.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-300-rise-of-the-yamato-state, claim TL:JPN:event:300:rise-of-the-yamato-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Introduction of Buddhism
claims.summary: Buddhism reaches Japan from the Korean kingdom of Baekje, traditionally dated to 552; it is championed by the Soga clan over conservative opposition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-538-introduction-of-buddhism, claim TL:JPN:event:538:introduction-of-buddhism, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Prince Shotoku's Seventeen-Article Constitution
claims.summary: As regent, Prince Shotoku promulgates a set of Confucian and Buddhist moral precepts for government and intensifies the adoption of Chinese institutions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-604-prince-shotoku-s-seventeen-article-constitution, claim TL:JPN:event:604:prince-shotoku-s-seventeen-article-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Taika Reform
claims.summary: A court coup destroys Soga dominance and inaugurates reforms reorganizing land and administration along centralized Chinese lines, the basis of the ritsuryo state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-645-the-taika-reform, claim TL:JPN:event:645:the-taika-reform, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capital established at Nara
claims.summary: The court founds Japan's first permanent capital, Heijo-kyo (Nara), modeled on the Tang Chinese capital, beginning the Nara period.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-710-capital-established-at-nara, claim TL:JPN:event:710:capital-established-at-nara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capital moved to Heian-kyo (Kyoto)
claims.summary: Emperor Kanmu relocates the capital to Heian-kyo, the site of Kyoto, opening the Heian period and a long era of aristocratic court culture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-794-capital-moved-to-heian-kyo-kyoto, claim TL:JPN:event:794:capital-moved-to-heian-kyo-kyoto, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Tale of Genji
claims.summary: The court lady Murasaki Shikibu completes The Tale of Genji, widely regarded as the world's first full-length novel and the summit of Heian literature.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1010-the-tale-of-genji, claim TL:JPN:event:1010:the-tale-of-genji, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Genpei War
claims.summary: Civil war between the Taira and Minamoto warrior clans ends with Minamoto victory at Dan-no-ura in 1185, shattering court supremacy and ushering in warrior rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1180-genpei-war, claim TL:JPN:event:1180:genpei-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Minamoto Yoritomo becomes shogun
claims.summary: Yoritomo is appointed shogun, formalizing the Kamakura shogunate and a system of warrior government that would last, in varying forms, until 1868.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1192-minamoto-yoritomo-becomes-shogun, claim TL:JPN:event:1192:minamoto-yoritomo-becomes-shogun, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mongol invasions repelled
claims.summary: Kublai Khan's Yuan forces twice attempt to invade Japan; both fleets are wrecked by typhoons later mythologized as the kamikaze, or divine winds.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1274-mongol-invasions-repelled, claim TL:JPN:event:1274:mongol-invasions-repelled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ashikaga Takauji founds the Muromachi shogunate
claims.summary: Takauji establishes the second shogunate, ruling from Kyoto's Muromachi district and presiding over a brilliant if unstable cultural era.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1338-ashikaga-takauji-founds-the-muromachi-shogunate, claim TL:JPN:event:1338:ashikaga-takauji-founds-the-muromachi-shogunate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Onin War
claims.summary: A succession dispute ignites a decade of warfare that devastates Kyoto, cripples shogunal authority, and tips Japan into the fragmented Sengoku era.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1467-onin-war, claim TL:JPN:event:1467:onin-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arrival of Europeans and firearms
claims.summary: Portuguese traders reach Japan, introducing firearms and, soon after, Christianity, adding new pressures to the Sengoku wars.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1543-arrival-of-europeans-and-firearms, claim TL:JPN:event:1543:arrival-of-europeans-and-firearms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hideyoshi completes unification
claims.summary: Toyotomi Hideyoshi brings the last domains under central control, finishing the reunification of Japan begun by Oda Nobunaga.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1590-hideyoshi-completes-unification, claim TL:JPN:event:1590:hideyoshi-completes-unification, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Sekigahara
claims.summary: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeats a rival coalition in the decisive battle that makes him master of Japan and clears the path to the shogunate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1600-battle-of-sekigahara, claim TL:JPN:event:1600:battle-of-sekigahara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tokugawa shogunate founded
claims.summary: Ieyasu is appointed shogun and establishes his government at Edo, beginning the Tokugawa (Edo) period of long internal peace.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1603-tokugawa-shogunate-founded, claim TL:JPN:event:1603:tokugawa-shogunate-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sakoku: national seclusion
claims.summary: A series of edicts seals Japan from most foreign contact, banning Christianity and overseas travel and restricting trade to Nagasaki for over two centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1639-sakoku-national-seclusion, claim TL:JPN:event:1639:sakoku-national-seclusion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Meiji Restoration
claims.summary: A coup ends the Tokugawa shogunate and restores direct imperial rule under Emperor Meiji, launching rapid modernization and Westernization.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1868-meiji-restoration, claim TL:JPN:event:1868:meiji-restoration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Meiji Constitution promulgated
claims.summary: Japan adopts a Western-influenced constitution establishing a constitutional monarchy with an imperial parliament, the Diet.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1889-meiji-constitution-promulgated, claim TL:JPN:event:1889:meiji-constitution-promulgated, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Russo-Japanese War
claims.summary: Japan's victory over Russia marks the first modern defeat of a European power by an Asian state and confirms Japan as a major power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1904-russo-japanese-war, claim TL:JPN:event:1904:russo-japanese-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
claims.summary: Japan attacks the U.S. fleet at Pearl Harbor, bringing the United States into World War II and opening the Pacific War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Japan: Imperial myth, borrowed continental learning, and centuries of warrior rule braided into a singular modern state.", terralore.co/country/JPN/chronicle#ev-1941-attack-on-pearl-harbor, claim TL:JPN:event:1941:attack-on-pearl-harbor, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Atomic bombings and surrender
claims.summary: The United States drops atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki on August 6 and 9; Japan announces surrender, formalized on September 2, ending World War II.

claims.summary: A magnitude-9.0 earthquake and tsunami devastate northeastern Japan and trigger meltdowns at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant.
